restoration_note: Teaching 78 enumerates four great works of self-love (appetite of mouth, fornication, wealth-with-boasting, war/dominion) and contrasts them with the soul that receives the discrimination of light from darkness, beautiful from bad. Most gaps are formulaic: ordinal completions (ⲧⲧϣⲁⲣⲡ, ⲧⲧⲙⲁϩⲥⲛⲉⲩ, etc.), repetitions of ⲛⲉⲩⲉⲣⲏⲩ 'one another', relative converters ⲛⲉⲧϣⲟⲟⲡ, and the chapter's framing 'all men of the earth kill one another' phrase — all secure. Medium lacunae for the four works' nouns (ⲡⲣⲁⲩϣ 'care', ⲡⲉⲁⲩ 'glory', ⲡⲍⲏⲩ 'gain', ⲙⲛⲧⲣⲙⲙⲁⲟ 'wealth') were restored from the spiritual reading's articulation of each work, with moderate-to-low confidence. Five gaps left unrestorable: {19} (1-char fragment at line break), {24}–{25} (the connector between cosmos and the slaughtering clause), and {29}–{30} (the noun describing what the regenerated soul is established forth from — possibly ⲧⲉⲡⲣⲟⲃⲟⲗⲏ or ⲧⲉⲡⲱⲣϫ̄ but split unsecured).
